I submitted a message to PepsiCo informing them of my boycott in light of the CEO's comments. I just received an email an I feel that it clears up a few things and it was nice to see the media called out. Pasted below is the message that was received:

Dear Gabriel, Thank you for writing.

A big reason why the public’s trust in the mainstream media has declined in recent years is that coverage is too often based on inaccurate or incomplete reporting. Unfortunately, much of the coverage of Indra Nooyi’s recent comments reflects this reality, as numerous outlets chose to present her remarks in a fashion that captured neither the spirit of her message nor the context in which they were given. For example, you would never know from the headlines that the very first thing she did when the topic of the election came up was to congratulate President-elect Trump. She also highlighted three primary points of his agenda.

The following are excerpts from the discussion that provide a more complete view of her statements.

  • "First of all, I want to congratulate President-elect Donald Trump."

  • “We will all come together and unify the country."

  • "At some point, we’re going to have to pick up the big issues of technological unemployment, global trade, immigration — all of which needs reform."

At the same time, several outlets also completely misquoted her and/or took her statements totally out of context. For example, some articles quoted Mrs. Nooyi as saying, “How dare you talk about women this way,” implying she was speaking about or to the President-elect. She in fact never said this.

What she did say, in response to a broad question about the treatment of women in society, was: “How dare we talk about women that way. Why do we talk that way about a whole group of citizens?” It’s troubling, but perhaps not surprising, that some have chosen to change her words in an effort to manufacture controversy.

Having said all this, Mrs. Nooyi acknowledged through a spokesperson to the Washington Post that she misspoke when she said “all” employees were apprehensive about the outcome of the election. She was referring to the reaction of a group of employees she spoke to, and she never intended to imply that all employees feel the same way. She added that PepsiCo is "incredibly proud of the diverse views and backgrounds across our workforce, and we are united in our desire for a brighter future."

Lastly, it’s worth noting that, the morning after the election, Mrs. Nooyi sent a letter to PepsiCo employees making the following points:

  • "Yesterday, across this country, Americans turned out in record numbers to make their voices heard. I want to congratulate President-elect Donald Trump on his victory, and I wish him all the best as he begins the work of stewarding this country in the months and years ahead."

  • "I do hope that starting today, we can begin the process of healing, the process of overcoming the divisions that have been exposed during this campaign. I hope that starting today, we can refocus on the work of forging a partnership with one another to build our common future."

  • “We are, first and foremost, Americans. We are, first and foremost, mothers and fathers, sons and daughters, who want a better life for ourselves and our families. And the only way of ushering in that better life, the only way of moving forward as a country, is by walking together, hand-in-hand.”

The recent coverage, while it may have made for clickable headlines, misrepresented Mrs. Nooyi’s views.

Thanks again for writing. We hope this further information is helpful.

PepsiCo Consumer Relations
